analysis:
Integration of the 18 units: the PR is CI-routing only. In .github/workflows/provider-plan.yml (head ~183-185) it drops `required` from build-cluster, build-provider and cluster-release-checks, so while DARKBLOOM_JOB_SHAPES is off these lanes ask the Darkbloom plane without a size and get the approval's pinned macOS size instead of staying on Blacksmith. provider-tests.yml changes comments only (lines ~56-58, ~862-864). Docs (build.md, test.md), a changelog entry and the two CI test scripts (scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py PLAN_LANES and UNSIZED_PLAN_REQUEST, scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py regex at ~730 and ~828) are updated to match. The replayed patches are consistent across files: the workflow lane table, docs and test expectations all agree, and the script change loosens only the ' required' token in the route-line assertion.

No provider runtime, wire protocol, attestation, App Attest, key custody, encryption or prefix-cache code is touched, so A-001..A-020, TB-002/003/007/009/011/012 and T-041 are unaffected. The retained CI safeguards are unchanged and still asserted: top-level contents:read, persist-credentials:false, SHA-pinned actions, cache saves only on master/dev pushes, no secrets in provider jobs, fork PRs keep their fallback, exact label-array acceptance, HTTPS-only and certificate-verified plane contact, and release/signing/credentialed workflows on literal Blacksmith labels (UNROUTED list).

Residual, non-finding questions: (1) The build jobs produce test-product artifacts and caches, and now run on routed Darkbloom Sandbox runners in the sizes-off state. They already ran there when sizes were on, so this widens when routing applies rather than adding a capability. Runner isolation and trust of the Darkbloom plane, and the route logic itself, are not in the supplied evidence. (2) The replay is partial (45 units omitted), so the full provider-plan.yml cannot be confirmed. Cross-file consistency checks look fine and I identify no qualifying security regression.
